Subject: Launch spike — temporary commit uplift?

Hi Mateo,

Quick note — we have an upcoming feature launch the week of July 15 that will likely double our token usage for two months. We ran the projected load against the sandbox and confirmed the pattern (attached minimal extract). Can Redwood help with a short-term commit uplift or burst-bucket reshuffle to avoid overages? Would prefer not to renegotiate the annual price but happy to discuss a 6-month addendum or temporary burst credit.

Key asks:
- 2x monthly commit for July/August (then back to baseline)
- Larger burst pocket in the launch window for unexpected spikes
- Clear overage rate if we exceed the temporary uplift

Procurement copied for visibility (we may need a PO). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Nora Patel

N: +1 415-555-0134

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 1 Jul 2029 12:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Launch spike — temporary commit uplift?

Hi Nora — great to hear about the launch, congrats. Thanks for the usage extract. Short answer: yes, we can support a targeted, timeboxed uplift and a temporary reshuffle of the burst bucket.

I'll outline two practical options below so procurement can pick the one that maps to EdgeMap's billing flow:

Option A — Short-term commit addendum (recommended)
- Increase baseline monthly commit by 2x for a 2-month period (Jul 15 — Sep 14)
- Additive commitment billed pro-rata on the next invoice
- Overage rate during uplift: standard hosted overage rate at the committed tier (we can cap at N tokens for protection)

Option B — Burst-pocket credit + soft fallback
- Keep baseline commit; add a "launch burst pocket" (one-time credit) usable during Jul 15 — Sep 14
- If burst pocket exhausted, automatic fallback to baseline with overage at a slightly higher rate (we'll set a notification and soft throttling)

I attached a short proposal (EdgeMap_commit_proposal_v2.pdf) with line-item pricing for both options and an example invoice timing. From an ops perspective, Vanessa will validate capacity and the runtime routing for the period; Karthik, would you advise on whether we should reserve additional Dedicated slots or rely on hosted bursting?

If procurement wants a PO pre-signature, we can issue a commercial addendum and route a DocuSign link.

Next steps:
- Tell me preferred option (A or B)
- If A: confirm dates and preferred billing cadence; we’ll prepare addendum for signature
- If B: confirm desired burst credit amount and we’ll provision

Happy to join a 30-min call with procurement later this week.

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: EdgeMap_commit_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 22 pages, pricing appendix)

From: Nora Patel <nora.patel@edgemap.com>

Thanks Mateo — Option A looks cleaner for our finance team. A couple of quick clarifications before we loop procurement for PO:

1) If we commit to a 2x uplift for two months, will the invoice show a separate line for the uplift so our FP&A can reconcile it to the launch spend?
2) Can Redwood cap overage exposure for the uplift window (we'd like a hard cap rather than open-ended overage) — e.g., no more than a 15% overage on uplifted tokens?
3) DocuSign flow: procurement wants a single addendum we can sign; they prefer net30 on the uplift if possible.

If those are feasible, we can route a PO quickly. Thanks for turning this around.

Nora

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Hi Nora — I work on customer ops and will own the provisioning. Short answers inline: 

1) Yes — Option A invoices include a separate line item called "Temporary Commit Addendum" with dates and pro-rata amount so your FP&A can match it.
2) We can set a hard overage cap for the uplift window. Proposal: cap at 15% over the uplifted token amount, after which we shift to soft throttling and email alerts to your SREs. If you'd prefer guaranteed hard-stop throttling instead of overage billing, we can do that too — just confirm preference.
3) Net30 is fine for the uplift addendum; we'll reflect that in the addendum and the DocuSign packet.

Operational note: to avoid surprises, we'll enable a pre-launch alert channel (email + PagerDuty webhook optional) once the uplift goes live and a burn-rate dashboard in Redwood Console for the launch window. Please provide the SRE contact for the webhook.

Vanessa Ortiz
